reasons.U1: FLOW-1 step 1 gives only an intro with a one-line helper explanation ('도우미 설명 한 줄') plus a legend and caveat line; there is no real onboarding or explanation of how to read the numbers, and it is not raised as a question.
reasons.U2: Section 3 'Touch/keyboard' keeps tap-to-select plus a confirm button, makes list rows selectable and adds aria labels; FLOW-2 previews the win rate for a cell outside the candidates before confirming; FLOW-4 cancels pending work on confirm; FLOW-5 covers undo.
reasons.U3: The 390x844 'information budget' lists what must stay on screen (turn, 358px board, top 3 numbers, confirm button, the #1 line), what goes below the scroll (list with a 'more' toggle, reasons, caveat) and what is dropped (ranks 4-5 on the board, the full heatmap).
reasons.U4: FLOW-1 and FLOW-2 follow a turn from the user's side: see the candidates, tap a cell or row, compare ('이 자리 41% (추천 H9 62%)'), confirm, watch the predicted replies turn into the AI move, then see a 'same/different from prediction' note.
reasons.R1: Q1 lays out simulated win rate, an index, color bands or a raw % against the BRIEF conflict; section 3 shows the sample count, hides numbers under 30 games, and the caveat says 'not a real win rate against humans'.
reasons.R2: Q7 puts the wait-versus-accuracy trade-off to the user (progressive display, about 3s cap); section 3 sets separate budgets and keeps the 2s watchdog; FLOW-4 discards stale results; it notes low-end devices are unmeasured.
reasons.R3: Nine prioritized questions (Q1-Q9) go to the user one at a time, and the BRIEF conflict is left for the user to settle; only details the plan judges reversible are kept as owner decisions in section 3.
